clue.text: Formic indigestion remedy?

parts.note: formic acid is the acid of ants, so a cure for heartburn described as formic reads as an insect plus an acid

explanation.surface: A query about some formic-acid-based cure for an upset stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: Formic comes from Latin formica, ant: formic acid is literally ant acid, which split differently is a stomach remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet that neutralises stomach acid is the standard remedy for indigestion.

clue.text: School head dropped pointer

indicators.note: head dropped says the first letter of the school is removed

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: A headmaster lost the stick used for pointing.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a well-known English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is a sign used to point the way, a pointer.

clue.text: Tool for a timeserver

definitions.meaning: a cutting device for hedges or hair
someone who trims their opinions to suit the times

explanation.definitionFit: A trimmer cuts hedges or edges, and is also an opportunist who shifts views to suit the prevailing mood.

clue.text: Money in store for auditor

indicators.note: for auditor says what follows is heard rather than read, as a listener would

parts.note: a cache is a hidden store

explanation.surface: Funds held in a shop for the accountant to check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' looks like an accountant; here it means a listener, so CACHE is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: ready money in coins and notes is cash.

clue.text: A sad idea — Orlando may be defunct

indicators.note: may be says the letters could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: The setter fears a bad idea will finish him off.
explanation.walkthrough: Orlando is the setter's own pseudonym, used here as anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead as a doornail is an idiom for utterly dead, defunct.

clue.text: Not public transport backed by Parks?

indicators.note: backed says the word for transport is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: a bus is public transport
Rosa Parks, the American civil-rights figure who refused to give up her bus seat

explanation.surface: Something about private transport supported by the parks authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parks' looks like green spaces; it is Rosa Parks, whose first name gives ROSA. 'backed' turns BUS into SUB.
explanation.definitionFit: Sub rosa is Latin for 'under the rose', meaning secret or confidential, so not public.

clue.text: Mae West film for Sondheim, eh?

parts.note: the composer's name plus eh is what a garbled spelling of the title's first three words would produce

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Mae West movie would suit Stephen Sondheim.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: WRONG in the title acts as an anagram signal applied to SHEDONEHIM, which gives SONDHEIM EH.
explanation.definitionFit: She Done Him Wrong is a 1933 film starring Mae West.

clue.text: In Paris I turned up with a poet, without a painter

indicators.note: without means outside, so the poet goes around the rest

parts.note: Robert Burns, the Scottish poet

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue says the French word is read bottom to top

parts.note: je is French for I
a means one

explanation.surface: A Parisian story of meeting a poet but missing a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside: BURNS surrounds EJ (JE reversed by 'turned up') plus ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Burne-Jones was a Pre-Raphaelite painter.

clue.text: View duck on the wing

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
a pinion is a bird's wing

explanation.surface: Looking at a duck in flight.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman out for no runs scores a duck, the shape of an O.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view one holds.

clue.text: Gas supplied by northeast region of France

parts.note: argon is an inert gas

explanation.surface: Gas piped in from the northeast of France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argonne is a forested region of northeastern France.

clue.text: Gallery has prior checks put back

indicators.note: prior says the word for checks comes in front of the gallery

parts.note: reins check or restrain a horse
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A gallery has its earlier inspections returned.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of art galleries in London and elsewhere in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore someone or something to a former position is to put it back.

clue.text: One called out "Sorry!"

indicators.note: out has the word for called spread out so that the letter for one sits within it

parts.note: rung means telephoned, called
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone shouted an apology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'called out' reads as shouted, but 'called' is RUNG (as on the phone) and 'out' opens it up to take I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruing something means regretting it, being sorry about it.

clue.text: Softy starts to wail, infuriating many people

indicators.note: starts to says take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A crybaby whose wailing annoys a lot of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A wimp is a feeble, timid person, a softy.

clue.text: Ivanhoe ran amok like George III

indicators.note: running amok is going wild, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Scott's hero Ivanhoe went on a rampage like a mad king.
explanation.walkthrough: George III, famous for his madness, was of the House of Hanover; 'ran amok' points at his reputed insanity.
explanation.definitionFit: George III belonged to the Hanoverian dynasty of British monarchs.

clue.text: Exams taken to heart — with this end result

parts.note: finals are the last university examinations
the core is the heart of something

explanation.surface: Exams taken seriously lead to this outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken to heart' looks like an idiom, but 'heart' gives CORE added to FINALS.
explanation.definitionFit: A final score is the closing result of a match, the end result.

clue.text: Vehicle brought back from Nagasaki or Tokyo

indicators.note: brought back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A car shipped home from one of two Japanese cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' marks the letters as lifted out of NagasAKI OR Tokyo; 'brought back' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: A troika is a Russian carriage or sleigh drawn by three horses, a vehicle.

clue.text: Measure cat, say

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure of width
the ounce is the snow leopard, a big cat

explanation.surface: An instruction to take a cat's measurements, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To enounce is to pronounce or state, an old word for say.

clue.text: Herb turned ass round

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: turned says the word for ass is read backwards

parts.note: an onager is a wild ass

explanation.surface: A plant that turned a donkey around.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a culinary herb related to marjoram.

clue.text: Where patients may be making progress?

definitions.text: Where patients may be making progress?

parts.words: Where patients may be making progress
parts.note: patients recover in hospital rooms, so a phrase for being on such rooms doubles as a word for going forward

explanation.definitionFit: Onwards means forward, making progress, and on wards is where hospital patients lie.

clue.text: Feeling expressed primarily by poet

indicators.note: primarily says take only the opening letter of the word

parts.note: Andrew Motion, Poet Laureate 1999-2009

explanation.surface: Sentiment voiced mainly by a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Motion was Britain's Poet Laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a strong sentiment such as joy or anger is an emotion.

clue.text: One airline no longer going to Mississippi for supporters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
BEA was British European Airways, merged into British Airways in 1974
MS is the postal abbreviation for Mississippi

explanation.surface: A defunct airline once flew to Mississippi for its backers.
explanation.walkthrough: BEA, British European Airways, ceased in 1974 when it merged into BA.
explanation.definitionFit: I-beams are steel girders with an I-shaped section, used as structural supports.

clue.text: Scottish king married to a college girl

parts.note: Beth is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A Scottish king wed to a student.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth was an eleventh-century king of Scotland, made famous by Shakespeare.

clue.text: They fix crossword we solved right away

indicators.note: solved suggests the letters are worked out into a new order
away says the letter for right is taken out

explanation.surface: Fixers sorting out a crossword we finished at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately', but it removes R from CROSSWORD; the rest with WE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood screws are fasteners that fix things to timber.

clue.text: Part of NT's functions?

definitions.meaning: the ... of the Apostles is a book of the New Testament
deeds or doings, the things one performs

explanation.definitionFit: Acts is a New Testament book, and acts are also performances or operations, functions.

clue.text: Washington's uncle accepting extremely large place near Boston

indicators.note: accepting says one piece takes in the other

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the US government in Washington

indicators.note: extremely says take the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A relative in Washington admits a big place in Massachusetts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely large' looks like 'huge' but gives L and E, the first and last letters of large.
explanation.definitionFit: Salem is a town in Massachusetts near Boston, famous for its witch trials.

clue.text: Need spin for PM

indicators.note: spin says the letters of the word are whirled into a new order

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister needs a spin doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin' rearranges the letters of NEED. Anthony Eden was British Prime Minister 1955-57.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Eden held office as British Prime Minister from 1955 to 1957, so PM fits by example.

clue.text: Old bread for an animal

definitions.meaning: dated British slang for money, as bread is
the rhinoceros, a large horned beast

explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is old slang for cash and also short for the horned African and Asian beast.

clue.text: Much first-rate upright timber

parts.note: A, as in A-grade, means top quality
an upright person is good, virtuous
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: Excellent vertical wooden posts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upright timber' looks like a single wooden post, but it splits into two separate pieces; deal is the British name for softwood planks.
explanation.definitionFit: A good deal is an idiom meaning a large amount, much.

clue.text: Article written in city about fish

indicators.note: written in says the article is put inside the other piece
about says the city's name is turned round

parts.note: Leeds is a city in Yorkshire
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece in a city's paper is about fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the city round, and 'written in' puts the article inside the result; the surface's newspaper article is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: The sand eel is a small slender sea fish that burrows in sand.

clue.text: Material used in packaging hamburgers

indicators.note: used in says the letters are found running inside the following words

explanation.surface: Cloth that wraps fast-food burgers.
explanation.definitionFit: Gingham is a checked cotton fabric, a material.
